text:
jing: Heads up — ran full eval for rw-7b-v2 after the calibration tweak (calib-id: c2026f) and seeing p95 token latency up ~2.6x and failures on structured JSON checks. Repro steps at the end.

alex: ugh. which change was flipped? per-layer clipping or the stochastic FP8 switch? :eyes: 

jing: both — we enabled stochastic fp8 on a subset of attention layers and tightened per-layer scale clipping. Profiler shows a kernel switch to a slow fallback on 3 attention layers for seq_len > 1024 (matmul_fp8_stochastic -> matmul_fp8_fallback). trace=0x9fa7b.

maria: can you paste the profiler summary and the batcher config? we recently bumped max_batch_tokens to 8192 in schedule-v3. might interact with kernel heuristics.

jing: PROFILER SUMMARY:
```
kernel_dispatch: matmul_fp8_stochastic (fast) 35% -> matmul_fp8_fallback 58%
p95_token_time: 45.2ms -> 118.7ms
kv_cache: extra memcpy per token ~1.1ms (aligned copies falling back)
mem:  CUDA memcpy synchronous spikes at layer 6,9,12
```

sam: that extra memcpy per step smells like KV cache layout/stride issues. calibration changed quant tables, which can change packing and cause non-coalesced copies. also could force scalar codepath in the batcher when it sees mixed-precision layers.

alex: we're also seeing quality diffs: structured-json tests show missing/empty fields. example: expected "steps": [..] got "steps": null in ~12% of cases. hallucinations on numeric fields (order_id => random digits).

maria: numeric skew could push logits toward early EOS or change generation length. do we have examples where only quant mode differs?

jing: yes — local diff on a 50-prompt micro-eval: reference vs calib=c2026f shows 8 prompts with truncated arrays, 4 with altered numeric tokens. attaching short repro snippet.

perf-bot: Telemetry alert: rollout c2026f -> p95 > 85ms, json-parse-failures +0.9% in canary.

devbot: created issue #4321 and assigned to @sam and @jing. Labels: perf, regression, quantization, oncall.

sam: triage plan: 1) reproduce on debug build with CUDA_KERNEL_LOG=1 to capture kernel selection path; 2) force mixprec=off to confirm revert both perf+quality; 3) run calibration using per-tensor clamp (vs per-layer) to compare quality deltas; 4) microbench KV memcpy for different alignments/batch shapes.

alex: add a temporary kernel-selection override to prefer tensorcore path even when stochastic enabled — I want to see if heuristic mis-detection is causing fallback.

maria: I'll run the full gold eval-suite overnight (50 golden prompts + schema checks) comparing calib c2025z (prev) vs c2026f.

jing: repro command: ```python repro.py --model rw-7b-v2 --calib c2026f --seq 1536 --batch 4 --dump-trace trace_0x9fa7b.log```

sam: if KV layout misalignment is root cause, fast fix is to restore previous packing for canary while we iterate on a proper vectorized memcpy patch. if it's kernel choice, we may revert stochastic flip.

maria: ops — can we pause the canary? current rollout at 2%.

ops-bot: Canary paused for rw-7b-v2 at 2%. Pinned rollout to calib c2025z.

alex: good. keep this channel updated with profiler logs and the eval diffs. once reproducible, we should add a targeted unit test for JSON-struct outputs under quant runs.

jing: adding logs to the issue and will kick off the debug repro now. thanks all. :thumbsup:
